item.title: Forget the iPhone Duo and Z Fold 8 – this foldable has it all
item.dc:content:
Cars. Smart Home. Leica-powered cameras. You may have heard of Xiaomi for many reasons, but unless you’re in China, folding phones probably aren't one of them. Yet the company has been releasing foldables since 2021, experimenting with both flip and book-style designs as it dialed in on what customers actually wanted.

Like Samsung and the Galaxy Z Fold 8, that search led to the passport-style Xiaomi 18 Fold, which launched days after Apple announced its own wide foldable. In true Xiaomi fashion, the result is uniquely Xiaomi in both fantastic and not-so-fantastic ways. It feels immediately familiar given its near symmetry with the iPhone Duo, yet it solves some of my biggest complaints with both Apple and Samsung’s foldables.

Both rivals set a precedent that passport-style foldables require compromises compared to traditional flagships. While Xiaomi had to make choices too, it made them in all the right places: battery and cameras. Instead of a smaller cell, you get a 6,000mAh beast – the largest in this form factor. Instead of a dual-lens setup without a telephoto, you get a flagship Leica triple camera complete with a 200MP main sensor and a 3.5x optical periscope telephoto.

However, the reverse also holds true. Xiaomi’s hardware-first R&D focus – combined with its lack of a global release – means HyperOS 4 lacks the UX refinement and Western polish other brands prioritize. To its credit, Xiaomi made it easy to install Google services and the Play Store, and its take on multitasking is genuinely unique. Still, a couple of daily essentials don't work as intended, and power-user staples like a desktop mode are missing despite support for wired display out.

In a nutshell, the Xiaomi 18 Fold pairs the best hardware in a passport-style foldable with software that falls short in familiar areas.

Call it Xiaomi’s Choice: do you want the absolute best hardware, or slightly lesser hardware with a much more refined software experience? Hardware nerd that I am, its appeal is obvious – though the iPhone Duo being as good as it is makes this a much closer fight than I anticipated.

Xiaomi 18 Fold Price, Specs & Availability

In mainland China, the Xiaomi 18 Fold starts at 10,999 yuan (roughly $1,640) – undercutting both the $1,899 Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the $1,999 iPhone Duo on paper before grey-market import markups eat into the savings.

More frustrating, Xiaomi hosted its global launch event for the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max earlier this week, conspicuously leaving the 18 Fold behind as a China-only release. This may change in future launches, but sadly, the Xiaomi 18 Fold looks set to remain China-exclusive.

Design, Hinge & Ergonomics

Pick up the Xiaomi 18 Fold, then the iPhone Duo, and the weight difference jumps out immediately. At 219g, Xiaomi's foldable is a full 35g lighter than Apple's first foldable – and only 18g heavier than the Galaxy Z Fold 8, despite cramming in a massive battery and periscope optics. Finished in a stunning matte Nishino Red glass against a dark metal frame, it looks and feels every bit like a premium flagship smartphone.

Looking at raw thickness alone actually sells Xiaomi's engineering short. When you calculate total folded volume, the Xiaomi 18 Fold (105.37 cm³) takes up roughly 6 percent less physical space than the iPhone Duo (111.95 cm³) and even edges out the razor-thin, tall-bodied Oppo Find N6 (105.82 cm³). Only the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (98.43 cm³) and Honor Magic V6 (102.15 cm³) feature smaller overall footprints – and neither offers the combination of a 6,000mAh battery and a periscope telephoto inside a pocket-friendly passport-style chassis.

Even the wide horizontal camera bar works in its favor. Rather than getting in the way, as some have complained, that housing doubles as a natural finger rest and grip mount, giving your index finger a solid ledge to anchor against when using the phone unfolded in portrait mode.

The keel hinge feels sturdy and reassuring, even if it lacks the iPhone Duo's crisp magnetic snap and holds fewer intermediate flex angles. Unlocking is fast and reliable via the side-mounted fingerprint reader, or 2D face unlock – a welcome convenience Apple skipped on the Duo.

There are inevitably trade-offs in a body that’s just 5.02mm thin when unfolded. The stereo speakers get plenty loud, but they lack low-end warmth and sound noticeably tinny and treble-heavy compared to Samsung and Apple. Unlike the iPhone Duo, it lacks stylus support, and its IP58 rating means it handles water submersion well but lacks the full dust protection of the iPhone Duo.

Displays

Like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and iPhone Duo, the wider passport aspect ratio transforms how usable the 18 Fold feels closed. The 5.38-inch cover screen is wide enough for comfortable two-thumb typing without feeling cramped, though it is a touch wide (but manageable) for single-handed use and the heavily rounded outer corners cut slightly more into usable corner real estate than the iPhone Duo's squared-off edges.

Unfold it, and the 7.58-inch inner OLED is a stunner. With HDR brightness pushing well past 3,700 nits, I’ve had no issues with outdoor visibility in harsh lighting.

Then there’s the crease. There’s no optical illusion here, as Apple has deployed. Instead, the crease virtually disappears straight-on, but is noticeable at sharper viewing angles – and sensitive eyes may notice low-brightness PWM flicker late at night.

Performance & Battery Life

The Xiaomi 18 Fold is more than just Xiaomi’s first passport-style foldable; it is also the first phone powered by Xiaomi’s new in-house flagship 3nm XRing O3 chip, paired with 16GB of LPDDR6 RAM.

In everyday use, it is blisteringly fast, flying through camera processing and split-screen multitasking without a stutter. Push it hard with sustained 3D gaming or prolonged camera sessions, though, and the thin chassis warms up noticeably along the upper half.

Whatever thermal efficiency trade-offs the XRing O3 makes, the 6,000mAh silicon-carbon battery renders them irrelevant. Endurance is class-leading, easily clearing a day of heavy testing. The smaller display sizes – especially the front display – mean lower power draw, with a key net result: the Xiaomi 18 Fold offers the best battery life of any foldable that I’ve tested so far.

When you finally need a top-up, 67W wired charging gets you to 50 percent in 19 minutes and a full charge in 50 minutes (with the brick included in the box). A charge rate of 120 mAh/min means you won’t be left short, and 50W wireless charging also lets you charge fairly quickly without wires.

Xiaomi 18 Fold Cameras

Xiaomi’s hardware-first R&D pays off most on the back. While Apple and Samsung both skipped an optical telephoto lens on their passport foldables, Xiaomi squeezed a 200MP main sensor, a 50MP ultrawide, and a dedicated 50MP 3.5x optical periscope telephoto into the 18 Fold.

As I saw during my head-to-head Dubai Marina camera shootout against the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8, that periscope lens isn't a minor spec-sheet win – it is a blowout. From 3x all the way past 30x, the 18 Fold resolves real optical detail where Apple and Samsung smear into digital mush, while Leica Vibrant color tuning and disciplined low-light metering make it the most consistent shooter of the three passport-style foldables.

The only real camera compromises are a narrower 17mm ultrawide that crops tighter than its rivals and a cover selfie lens that flares in harsh backlighting. Otherwise, this is the closest a squat foldable has come to a true flagship camera system. To dive deeper into the camera, head over to our passport-style foldable camera shootout – you can see some of the zoom examples from that comparison above!

Software: Held Back by Borders

Living with HyperOS 4 (based on Android 17) is a study in contradictions. Strip away the import context, and the software is genuinely lovely to use day to day; animations are fluid, and the UI feels snappy.

Xiaomi's six-app horizontal multitasking strip lets you line up three full-height panes at once while swiping across half a dozen open apps. It’s impressive, and on par with the Oppo Find N6 for the best multitasking on a foldable.

HyperOS 4 makes it effortless to install Google services, with all the underlying frameworks included out of the box: I have been running the Play Store and the Gemini app on here without a hitch. However, because this device is built strictly for mainland China, several deeply integrated Android features break down in day-to-day usage. It won’t let you swap the default system assistant to launch Gemini, nor change the default browser across the system to Chrome.

Then there are Google services. Find Hub shows the device, but can never find its location, even after enabling every background permission. The same applies to Google’s 2FA – when you sign into your Android phone on an existing device, it’ll often prompt you to verify with your existing device. On the Xiaomi 18 Fold, these alerts never appear, even after opening any of Google’s apps.

Then there are two issues common to China-only devices for years. Android Auto simply does not work, and like many China-specific phones, there’s no support for eSIM. This isn’t strictly Xiaomi’s fault, as China only approved eSIMs after Apple forced the issue last year with the eSIM-only iPhone Air launch.

Despite supporting wired video out over USB-C, Xiaomi still omits a desktop mode, third-party app scaling occasionally leaves awkward borders on the 4.24:3 screen, and it doesn't support 6 GHz Wi-Fi.

The frustrating part is how easy the fix would be. Xiaomi just needs to follow Oppo's playbook and pair the 18 Fold with the Western HyperOS ROM it already shipped globally on the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max: doing so would wipe out nearly every one of these headaches overnight.

Should You Buy the Xiaomi 18 Fold?

If you want the best hardware in a foldable this size and you can live with the software compromises and compatibility issues, look no further than the Xiaomi 18 Fold. By pairing a pocketable 219g passport body with a 6,000mAh battery and a Leica periscope camera, Xiaomi proved you don't have to sacrifice flagship hardware for a wide foldable.

That brings us right back to Xiaomi's Choice. If you live in China – or you are an enthusiast willing to import a phone and live without Android Auto, eSIMs, and Find Hub tracking – this is the finest piece of foldable hardware you can buy.

For everyone else, the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8 remain the safer, far better-integrated daily drivers – even though the hardware is considerably less impressive – at least until Xiaomi finally gives its best foldable the global ROM it deserves.

Personally, the smaller size, excellent battery life, and that telephoto lens mean the Xiaomi 18 Fold will definitely be in my arsenal during trade shows and other work events, even if I keep using the iPhone Duo as my daily passport-style foldable.

When you calculate total folded volume, the Xiaomi 18 Fold (105.37 cm³) takes up roughly 6 percent less physical space than the iPhone Duo (111.95 cm³) and even edges out the razor-thin, tall-bodied Oppo Find N6 (105.82 cm³). Only the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (98.43 cm³) and Honor Magic V6 (102.15 cm³) feature smaller overall footprints – and neither offers the combination of a 6,000mAh battery and a periscope telephoto inside a pocket-friendly passport-style chassis.

Even the wide horizontal camera bar works in its favor. Rather than getting in the way, as some have complained, that housing doubles as a natural finger rest and grip mount, giving your index finger a solid ledge to anchor against when using the phone unfolded in portrait mode.

The keel hinge feels sturdy and reassuring, even if it lacks the iPhone Duo's crisp magnetic snap and holds fewer intermediate flex angles. Unlocking is fast and reliable via the side-mounted fingerprint reader, or 2D face unlock – a welcome convenience Apple skipped on the Duo.

There are inevitably trade-offs in a body that’s just 5.02mm thin when unfolded. The stereo speakers get plenty loud, but they lack low-end warmth and sound noticeably tinny and treble-heavy compared to Samsung and Apple. Unlike the iPhone Duo, it lacks stylus support, and its IP58 rating means it handles water submersion well but lacks the full dust protection of the iPhone Duo.

Displays

Like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and iPhone Duo, the wider passport aspect ratio transforms how usable the 18 Fold feels closed. The 5.38-inch cover screen is wide enough for comfortable two-thumb typing without feeling cramped, though it is a touch wide (but manageable) for single-handed use and the heavily rounded outer corners cut slightly more into usable corner real estate than the iPhone Duo's squared-off edges.

Unfold it, and the 7.58-inch inner OLED is a stunner. With HDR brightness pushing well past 3,700 nits, I’ve had no issues with outdoor visibility in harsh lighting.

Then there’s the crease. There’s no optical illusion here, as Apple has deployed. Instead, the crease virtually disappears straight-on, but is noticeable at sharper viewing angles – and sensitive eyes may notice low-brightness PWM flicker late at night.

Performance & Battery Life

The Xiaomi 18 Fold is more than just Xiaomi’s first passport-style foldable; it is also the first phone powered by Xiaomi’s new in-house flagship 3nm XRing O3 chip, paired with 16GB of LPDDR6 RAM.

In everyday use, it is blisteringly fast, flying through camera processing and split-screen multitasking without a stutter. Push it hard with sustained 3D gaming or prolonged camera sessions, though, and the thin chassis warms up noticeably along the upper half.

Whatever thermal efficiency trade-offs the XRing O3 makes, the 6,000mAh silicon-carbon battery renders them irrelevant. Endurance is class-leading, easily clearing a day of heavy testing. The smaller display sizes – especially the front display – mean lower power draw, with a key net result: the Xiaomi 18 Fold offers the best battery life of any foldable that I’ve tested so far.

When you finally need a top-up, 67W wired charging gets you to 50 percent in 19 minutes and a full charge in 50 minutes (with the brick included in the box). A charge rate of 120 mAh/min means you won’t be left short, and 50W wireless charging also lets you charge fairly quickly without wires.

Xiaomi 18 Fold Cameras

Xiaomi’s hardware-first R&D pays off most on the back. While Apple and Samsung both skipped an optical telephoto lens on their passport foldables, Xiaomi squeezed a 200MP main sensor, a 50MP ultrawide, and a dedicated 50MP 3.5x optical periscope telephoto into the 18 Fold.

As I saw during my head-to-head Dubai Marina camera shootout against the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8, that periscope lens isn't a minor spec-sheet win – it is a blowout. From 3x all the way past 30x, the 18 Fold resolves real optical detail where Apple and Samsung smear into digital mush, while Leica Vibrant color tuning and disciplined low-light metering make it the most consistent shooter of the three passport-style foldables.

The only real camera compromises are a narrower 17mm ultrawide that crops tighter than its rivals and a cover selfie lens that flares in harsh backlighting. Otherwise, this is the closest a squat foldable has come to a true flagship camera system. To dive deeper into the camera, head over to our passport-style foldable camera shootout – you can see some of the zoom examples from that comparison above!

Software: Held Back by Borders

Living with HyperOS 4 (based on Android 17) is a study in contradictions. Strip away the import context, and the software is genuinely lovely to use day to day; animations are fluid, and the UI feels snappy.

Xiaomi's six-app horizontal multitasking strip lets you line up three full-height panes at once while swiping across half a dozen open apps. It’s impressive, and on par with the Oppo Find N6 for the best multitasking on a foldable.

HyperOS 4 makes it effortless to install Google services, with all the underlying frameworks included out of the box: I have been running the Play Store and the Gemini app on here without a hitch. However, because this device is built strictly for mainland China, several deeply integrated Android features break down in day-to-day usage. It won’t let you swap the default system assistant to launch Gemini, nor change the default browser across the system to Chrome.

Then there are Google services. Find Hub shows the device, but can never find its location, even after enabling every background permission. The same applies to Google’s 2FA – when you sign into your Android phone on an existing device, it’ll often prompt you to verify with your existing device. On the Xiaomi 18 Fold, these alerts never appear, even after opening any of Google’s apps.

Then there are two issues common to China-only devices for years. Android Auto simply does not work, and like many China-specific phones, there’s no support for eSIM. This isn’t strictly Xiaomi’s fault, as China only approved eSIMs after Apple forced the issue last year with the eSIM-only iPhone Air launch.

Despite supporting wired video out over USB-C, Xiaomi still omits a desktop mode, third-party app scaling occasionally leaves awkward borders on the 4.24:3 screen, and it doesn't support 6 GHz Wi-Fi.

The frustrating part is how easy the fix would be. Xiaomi just needs to follow Oppo's playbook and pair the 18 Fold with the Western HyperOS ROM it already shipped globally on the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max: doing so would wipe out nearly every one of these headaches overnight.

Should You Buy the Xiaomi 18 Fold?

If you want the best hardware in a foldable this size and you can live with the software compromises and compatibility issues, look no further than the Xiaomi 18 Fold. By pairing a pocketable 219g passport body with a 6,000mAh battery and a Leica periscope camera, Xiaomi proved you don't have to sacrifice flagship hardware for a wide foldable.

That brings us right back to Xiaomi's Choice. If you live in China – or you are an enthusiast willing to import a phone and live without Android Auto, eSIMs, and Find Hub tracking – this is the finest piece of foldable hardware you can buy.

For everyone else, the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8 remain the safer, far better-integrated daily drivers – even though the hardware is considerably less impressive – at least until Xiaomi finally gives its best foldable the global ROM it deserves.

Personally, the smaller size, excellent battery life, and that telephoto lens mean the Xiaomi 18 Fold will definitely be in my arsenal during trade shows and other work events, even if I keep using the iPhone Duo as my daily passport-style foldable.

item.title: Google sets hard deadline for the Nest app and smart display Assistant
item.dc:content:
Google is finally pulling the plug on two legacy smart home holdouts next year.

Starting January 25, 2027, Nest users will need to use Google Home to manage their compatible devices, per Google Home's support page. And that's not the only major change coming: Google Assistant is also being kicked out of smart speakers and displays later next year, making room for Gemini.

The Nest app shutdown is another step in Google’s long-running effort to bring its smart home products under one roof. The company says that consolidating everything under Google Home will allow it to concentrate its engineering, security, and feature development on a single platform instead of having two distinct experiences.

Most users will not have to manually move their devices. Google Home will automatically display compatible Nest thermostats, cameras, doorbells, Nest Protect smoke and CO alarms, and Nest x Yale locks. Existing settings, schedules, and camera video history will also carry over.

But video clips you’ve saved in the Nest web app won’t automatically transfer. Google recommends that before Jan. 25, users go to home.nest.com and use its one-click Download All option to save anything worth keeping.

There is also a separate deadline for migrating your account. Users who keep logging into an old Nest account must link it to a Google account by March 25, 2027. Anyone who misses that deadline faces the risk of losing their Nest account, data, and subscriptions as Google starts processing deletions.

Google Assistant is next on the chopping block

The Nest app is not the only familiar part of Google's smart home ecosystem that is planned to be retired. Starting August 2, 2027, Google Assistant will no longer be available on compatible speakers and smart displays, the company announced. Gemini for Home will take its place.

Gemini is able to converse more naturally, understand follow-up questions, and respond to complex requests without requiring users to remember specific voice commands — unlike the traditional Assistant.

Google Home also features customizable Favorites, better camera streaming, advanced automations, and expanded Matter device support. Existing customers of first-generation Nest Aware will be automatically upgraded to Google Home Premium Advanced at no cost.

At least on paper, the move should simplify management of Google’s smart home ecosystem.

item.title: Forget the Buds 3—Galaxy Buds 4 Pro deal drops it almost 30%, and I can hear the heart-pounding bass already
item.dc:content:
A good pair of earbuds with a new phone has become pretty common these days. It's like another accessory people can't seem to live without. Buying a new phone? Grab a pair of earbuds and maybe a watch. But good sound can be hard to come by.

Samsung launched its Galaxy Buds 4 Pro this year, and Amazon has already slashed them by almost 30% in a slew of Early Black Friday deals.

The Galaxy Buds 4 Pro offer a slight redesign of Samsung's previous aesthetic with silicone tips and a stabilizer to keep them in your ears. The Buds 4 Pro offer a sharp increase in audio clarity, along with voice and gesture controls.View Deal

The Galaxy Buds 4 Pro made waves this year, and they're ✅ recommended if you want earbuds with detailed sound. The Buds 4 Pro's two drivers support the SSC UHQ codec, which refines audio beyond the Buds 3. What's more, the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro offers a newer, wider woofer that covers 20% more space (meaning more room for clear, powerful sound). The device's ANC (active noise cancellation) has improved over the Buds 3 for an uninterrupted experience.

On the flip side, you can ❌ skip this deal if you often have trouble finding eartips that fit. The Galaxy Buds 4 Pro don't offer a great range of options for our ears. Some eartips might fit better than others, or you might have a completely opposite experience. It's become a gripe for us, too. Additionally, you can also avoid these buds if you need to upgrade your phone.

Much of the Buds 4 Pro's performance and features come from newer software. If you don't have one of the latest Samsung Galaxy or Android phones with the latest software, you'll miss out.

The Galaxy Buds 4 Pro were a welcome upgrade. Samsung packed up to 30 hours of battery life into the buds (with ANC off), along with six mics. Calls should capture your voice without much interruption. However, the sound-quality upgrades are what truly won consumers over this year. The Buds 4 Pro accounted for 90% of units sold this year in Samsung's Galaxy Buds 4 series. The device crossed over 100,000 units sold after launch.

Consumers enjoyed that "Pro" meant something with these buds. After spending some time with the buds, we couldn't help but appreciate the subtle changes. Samsung seemed to have paid enough attention to sound quality to make it crisp and clear. While you're speaking, the buds lower their volume, so your conversation and audio stay uninterrupted (if you want). What's more, Samsung placed its touch controls on the body of the earbuds, not the stem.

Also, the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro Black Friday deal drops the price to that of the regular Galaxy Buds 4 option. It's hard to ignore, given all the upgrades.

item.title: This Oura Ring 5 deal chopped off 25% ahead of Black Friday—perfect for all the holiday feasts
item.dc:content:
Smart rings quickly positioned themselves as a "health-first" device. That remains true today, as you can see in everything Oura has done with its smart rings.

If you're shopping for a few early Black Friday deals—especially ahead of all the holiday feasts—Amazon is here with a 25% discount on its latest Ring 5.

Oura Ring 5 (Silver - Size 7): was $399 now $299
The Oura Ring 5 is an incredibly thin, lightweight smart ring that you'll forget you're wearing. Its long battery life and automatic activity tracking make it seamless in your daily routine.View Deal

The Oura Ring 5 is ✅ recommended if you want a smart ring that feels "barely there." Compared to its previous generation, the Ring 5 is 40% thinner. So if you've ever been cautious about a smart ring, thinking they fit too tightly or are too heavy, the Ring 5 might change your mind. What's more, the various finishes for the Oura Ring 5 make it blend easily with your attire, from silver to gold.

You'd probably ❌ skip this deal if you're looking for heart rate data that's pinpoint. The Ring 5 is a good smart ring for capturing swaths of health information; however, in our experience, it's fallen flat during exercise. Heart data during intense workouts can be hit-or-miss, so it can feel a bit off. Additionally, Oura produced the Ring 5 in fewer sizes.

You might also skip the Ring 5 if you don't want to keep paying a subscription for some of the best features.

In our experience, the Oura Ring 5 performed well. With consistent daily use, the Ring 5 was barely noticeable, but a lot was happening behind the scenes. Though the device is 40% smaller, Oura didn't compromise on two key areas: battery life and performance. The Ring 5 features a battery life that lasts six to nine days, along with heart rate, blood oxygen, and a digital temperature sensor.

Then there's its workout experience. While, yes, its heart rate data capture can be a little wonky, wearing the ring isn't terrible. Users would typically notice the smart ring while working out with weights; however, that was more true for the Ring 4 in our experience. The Ring 5 hadn't given us the annoying issue of pinching our skin. The Oura Ring 5 gives users access to Oura Labs, Women's Health (Cycle Insights, Pregnancy Insights), Metabolic Health (Glucose Tracking, Meals), and more.

item.title: Is wide the next phone craze? The new Huawei Osta O1 Pro looks like a fat iPhone Air
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Huawei has officially launched its new OSTA sub-brand and its first phone, the OSTA O1 Pro, in China
  • As leaks suggested, the O1 Pro offers a unique wide-screen form factor
  • Prices start at 5699 CNY, which comes to roughly $855 or £650, though it is unlikely that this phone will even release in the West

Last week I reported that Huawei was set to launch a new sub-brand called OSTA, with its first phone being an interesting wide-screen model called the OSTA O1 Pro. As of today, everything has been made official — and the OSTA O1 Pro is available to order now via the Huawei VMALL site in China.

As reliable Weibo tipsters suggested, the OSTA O1 Pro does indeed boast a unique wide form factor. Thanks to a newly uploaded spec sheet, we now know that it has a 6.39-inch display with a 120Hz refresh rate, starts at 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, and is powered by the Kirin 9030S chipset – the same mid-range chip as the standard Huawei Pura 90.

The phone has a 7,000mAh battery, with support for 66W SuperCharge and 5W wired reverse charging, as well as 50W wireless charging when using a compatible charger. As for the cameras, the OSTA O1 Pro has a 200MP main shooter paired with a 50MP telephoto lens. There doesn't seem to be a dedicated ultra-wide or macro lens present. There is, however, a 50MP selfie camera on the front of the phone.

The OSTA O1 Pro is available in three colours: Starry Night Black, Nebula White, and Starlight Purple (though the latter is only offered in 16GB+512GB and 16GB+1TB configurations). Prices start at 5699 CNY for the most basic model, which comes to roughly $855 or £650.

Android Central's take: Will wide-screen phones come to the West?

The OSTA O1 Pro would be a pretty unexceptional mid-range phone, were it not for that unique wide-screen format. It almost looks like an iPhone Air, but fatter and more... compressed. That's not a bad thing either, as I think wider formats like this definitely have a place.

The popularity of the Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 (which is similarly stout) shows that Android users are certainly interested in trying form factors that are a bit more out there than the usual candy bar shape. The design of the OSTA O1 Pro also just looks like it would be very comfortable in the hands and fit comfortably in most pockets.

Wider aspect ratios have advantages when it comes to multitasking too, as they make it easier to view multiple windows side by side when using the phone horizontally.

The big question is whether the OSTA O1 Pro will make it to the West in any official capacity and, sadly, I don't think it's likely. Huawei pulled out of the US market following a US government ban in 2022 and has largely stopped selling its handsets in the UK as well. The only phones currently listed on the Huawei UK site are the Mate XT Ultimate Design and Mate X6 foldable, neither of which is actually available to buy on the store.

That said, we might still see other manufacturers come out with their own wide-screen model – especially if the OSTA O1 Pro proves popular with Chinese consumers.

item.title: This phone company launched a landline built for kids, and it's a safer, cheaper alternative to handing your child a smartphone
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Seattle-based brand Tin Can is launching its lineup of landline phones for kids in the UK soon
  • Each Tin Can phone works over Wi-Fi, ditching the screens and algorithms to encourage meaningful conversations between younger users
  • Calling other Tin Cans users is free, but you'll need to subscribe to call outside UK numbers, which can only be enabled through adult approval

Smartphones and social media have completely changed the way youngsters communicate and interact with each other, but one tech company wants to resurrect a classic method of communication so kids can chat with each other just like the good old days.

Seattle-based brand Tin Can has been reinventing the landline phone for the younger generation for the past two years, and now the kid-friendly mobile devices are finally making their UK debut on November 30, mimicking the design and feel of landline devices that are now a thing of the past. But these aren't fake Fisher-Price toys — these things actually work.

Vibrant and bold in design, Tin Can phones are wired to ensure your child has access to a safer means of communication. item.title: Amazon's new budget-friendly tablet has crashed down to under £100 in a lowest-ever price deal
item.dc:content:
It feels like tech everywhere is getting more and more expensive, but the Black Friday sales give you the opportunity to secure some rare bargains. If you're looking for a tablet and have a budget of just £100, then your options are usually extremely limited: entry-level models like the Lenovo Tab One or the Samsung Galaxy Tab A11 often go for more than £150.

Luckily, Amazon has come to the rescue with its brand-new Alexa Tablet line, which has seen a huge swathe of discounts in the ongoing early Black Friday sales. The cheapest option is the Amazon Alexa Tablet 8, the brand's entry-level model, which has plummeted to just £99.99 from £199.99 thanks to a massive 50% price cut.

Although the specs are modest, you're still getting a fully functional, working tablet for under £100, and in 2026 that's worth shouting about. The low price makes this a fantastic pick if you're shopping for kids, as you won't need to worry about them damaging something that will cost a huge amount to replace.

Despite the low cost, there are some premium elements to the design too. The case is a durable aluminium rather than plastic, and the chipset powering it all is the same MediaTek 8-Core processor found in the much pricier Alexa Tablet 11 and is capable of delivering reliable day-to-day performance.

  • Browse the full Amazon Black Friday Week sale

Alexa Tablet 8: was £199.99 now £99.99
Amazon's most basic Android tablet is a great little budget buy at under £100. The octa-core MediaTek SoC is perfect for most basic use cases, though the 64GB of storage and modest 4GB of RAM could be limitations if you intend to download a lot of apps or multitask often. Also be aware that this model comes with lock-screen ads by default, but you can at least pay a small fee to remove them.

Key specs at a glance: Display - 1340x800 60Hz LCD, RAM - 4GB, Storage - 64GB, SoC - octa-core MediaTek, MicroSD card slot - NoView Deal

✅Recommended if: you want a bargain-basement, compact tablet for basic day-to-day use or to give to the kids. With its modest specs, the Amazon Alexa Tablet 8 isn't going to be a good fit for power users – but if you just want to browse the web, respond to emails, read e-books, or watch movies via streaming, it will more than suffice.

The octa-core SoC and robust aluminium case also mean that it's better than some more expensive competitors in certain regards.

❌Skip this deal if: you require more storage or RAM, or want a better screen. The big limitations here are that it has 64GB of storage and 4GB of RAM. The storage unfortunately cannot be upgraded, as there is no microSD card slot, so you will likely run out of space quickly if you want to download Android apps. The RAM will also limit your ability to multitask.

Finally, the screen is just 1340x800 resolution – HD but not Full HD. It won't be too noticeable given the small 8.7-inch size, but might look a bit fuzzy to those with sharp eyes.

item.title: I regret buying the Sony WH-1000 XM5 instead of the XM4 — especially at this sub-$200 Black Friday price
item.dc:content:
Audiophiles, listen up; there are some great Sony headphone Black Friday deals already kicking about, but it's the previous-gen Sony WH-1000 XM4 model that's caught my attention.

Amazon is listing the Sony WH-1000 XM4 model for $198 from $299.99, knocking a generous $100 off what were one of our best wireless headphones at the time of release some six years ago. And yes, Sony has released two iterations since then — I've been using the WH-1000 XM5s for a few years and have no complaints — but there's a reason the XM4s are still a fan favorite.

Sony's XM5s, and more recently its WH-1000 XM6 headphones, have noticeable upgrades; the design is more ambitious and polished, and the audio quality is slightly more refined with each upgrade. But in the case of the XM4s, they boost audio performance that is way above satisfactory and not totally different from the XM5s, with above-average ANC that does the job at shutting out noise while on a commute.

But that's not the only reason why audiophiles still love them to this day. The headphones' folding ear pads, a hardware feature that was abandoned in the XM5 release, aren't just handy for reducing to a compact travel size but are a huge advantage for hardware care overall. Though the XM5s have served me well, they're quite bulky to travel with, meaning I don't bother using the travel case, which results in discoloration.

  • Browse all the latest Black Friday Amazon deals

WH-1000 XM4C headphones: was $299.99 now $198
The XM4C model is based on the previous-gen XM4 headphones, featuring updated sound tuning that packs pretty much the same audio standard as the XM5s, but is much cheaper and much more practical. We don't have a lot of price history to go off of, but this is the lowest price we've seen for this model in the past few months. View Deal

✅Recommended if: You're sticking to a budget and don't want to spend the best part of $300+ for a pair of Sony's latest headphones.

If you travel a lot and haven't got loads of space to carry around a bulky pair of headphones, the folding earpads reduce the headphones' size, so you can easily squeeze them into your bag. They also pack a solid battery life, making them ideal for longer journeys.

❌Skip this deal if: You have the money to spend and prefer the stylish aesthetics of the XM5 or XM6 headphones.

item.title: An affordable way into the Samsung ecosystem? The brand's best entry-level tablet is under $200 right now
item.dc:content:
You might associate Samsung with its high-end flagships, but the brand also makes plenty of good hardware aimed at more budget-conscious buyers. One such model is the Samsung Galaxy Tab A11+, a popular and relatively affordable 11-inch tablet that's on sale for under $200 at Amazon right now, despite specs that punch above that price point and reflect its usual going rate of around $300.

The 11-inch display comes in at a 1920x1200 resolution, which is perfect for streaming, and a 90Hz refresh rate for smoother scrolling. The octa-core MediaTek MT8775 is by no means the fastest chip around, but it is sufficient for day-to-day tasks like media consumption, web browsing, emailing, and some casual gaming. It's paired with 6GB of RAM too, so you can have a few tabs open at the same time without losing your progress thanks to an app refresh.

This under-$200 model ships with 128GB of storage, so enough for a few apps and some local videos, but there is thankfully a microSD card slot if you want to expand it in order to fit more downloaded media.

item.title: I’m saying goodbye to my old smart speaker in favor of the Echo Dot Max this Black Friday — all because it’s less than $100
item.dc:content:
The countdown to Black Friday 2026 is officially on, and with just seven days left until the madness hits, we're knee-deep in early deals across the best smart speakers and audio devices.

I've been a loyal Amazon Echo user ever since the tech giant first launched its family of smart home hubs, and my beloved Echo Pop has served me well for the past few years. But now that I've had time to appreciate good audio, I fear it's time to bid farewell, take the plunge, and treat myself to a long-overdue upgrade.

One of Amazon's most recent additions to its audio lineup, the Echo Dot Max, is now $84.99 down from $119.99 in the retailer's early Black Friday sale, and it's one of the company's biggest audio upgrades yet.

With a designated subwoofer and tweeter, the Echo Dot Max packs bass that is three times more robust than the Echo Dot (5th Gen). But despite its compact size, it doesn't fall short on performance, supporting Dolby Atmos and spatial audio, which is ideal for filling smaller spaces in your home or for stretching across large rooms.

Sound aside, the latest Echo range of speakers are the first devices native to the AI-powered Alexa+ which, with the help of the new AZ3 chip, offers faster, smarter responses to your prompts. Although the lineup was refreshed over a year ago, last year's Black Friday offers weren't as generous as they are this time around.

  • Browse all the latest Black Friday Amazon deals

Echo Dot Max (Glacier White): was $119.99 now $84.99
For less than $100, you can score one of Amazon's latest audio devices, and it's a serious upgrade from older models on the audio and smart home fronts. While it's not the lowest price we've seen (Prime Day beats it by $20), it's cheaper than last year's Black Friday listing, but whether it will get another price drop is another question. View Deal

✅Recommended if: You've been using an older Amazon Echo device for a long time and want to upgrade to a device with advanced inner workings. If you're looking for a device that's not only punchier on the audio side, but packs improved AI features and overall smarter home assistance, built-in Alexa+ will go a long way, especially if you have other Amazon devices such as a Ring doorbell.

❌Skip this deal if: Your previous-gen Echo speaker is running just fine, or you're not a massively keen audiophile. If you're a Prime Member, Alexa+ is available in your subscription and has been rolled out to older models, so you don't necessarily need to upgrade to a new device to take advantage of its smarts.

If you're in the Google smart home ecosystem and don't want to be a traitor, then the flagship Google Home Speaker is a solid alternative option, especially if you can find a good deal on it this Black Friday.

item.title: ‘The best speaker you can get for under 40 bucks’ — this super portable Bluetooth speaker is a holiday must-have
item.dc:content:
A small speaker doesn't have to mean small sound, and audio maker JBL is the king of squeezing a lot of volume out of a tiny package. The JBL Go 5 is one of the most compact models in its flagship lineup, but still brings plenty to the table.

It's the speaker that I personally rely on whenever I need to bring a super compact model with me on holiday or out and about, and now it could be yours for just $39.95 (down from $54.95) in the Best Buy Black Friday sale.

I've been browsing the early Black Friday sales extensively over the last few days, and for my money, this is by far the best speaker you can get for under 40 bucks in the sale. The sound is excellent given its small size; it's extremely durable thanks to a waterproof cloth and rubber construction, and it's even got a cool light feature with two bright bars that flash as your tunes play.

It also comes in a wide range of colors, from basic white and black to more exciting purple and baby blue, or even a cool camo (all of them have the same discount, so you can choose your favorite).

At this price, I would even consider getting two, as you can pair them up using the companion app for full stereo sound.

  • Browse all the latest Best Buy Black Friday 2026 deals

A cute, compact speaker that's perfect for your next vacation. The JBL Go 5 is waterproof, durable, offers up to 10 hours of battery life (with the Playtime Boost feature enabled), and is one of the very best-sounding options in this price range and form factor. It even has a robust companion app, and you can link two together for stereo sound. A range of colors is available at this price, so do take a moment to choose a favorite.View Deal

✅Recommended because: there are few alternatives that sound this good in this form factor and affordable price range, making the JBL Go 5 a fantastic all-round pick. The design is excellent, offering both durability and style, and even includes customizable lighting. You get a great companion app too, where you can customize its sound with a range of EQ presets or even create your own. Despite its small size, the battery is strong and offers up to 10 hours on a single charge.

❌Skip this deal if: you have a bigger budget for your speaker purchase, or want something with more punch. Although the JBL Go 5 is a standout given its rock-bottom price, if you pay more, you can get better sound.

The JBL Flip 7 would be my recommended mid-range alternative: it's larger and more expensive, but offers much richer audio and superior battery life. For at-home listening, something like the comparatively super high-end JBL Boombox 4 is also worth weighing up.

item.title: The Motorola Edge 2026 just hit its lowest price yet with a $200 Black Friday discount
item.dc:content:
Black Friday sales are officially underway, so if you’re tired of carrying around oversized phones in your pocket, now’s a good time to upgrade. The Motorola Edge 2026 answers that call with a small footprint, and it just got a lot easier on your wallet.

Right now, Amazon is offering the Motorola Edge 2026 for $399.99, a 33% discount from its normal $599.99 list price. That’s $200 off and the best price we’ve seen on this phone according to Amazon’s price history. Please note this offer is only available while stocks last.

The Motorola Edge 2026 combines a compact design with a bright AMOLED display and a large battery. At this price, you're getting a $200 saving and its lowest recorded price on Amazon.View Deal

✅ Recommended if: You want a small, light Android phone with a bright screen and good battery life for less than a flagship price.

❌ Skip this deal if: You want powerful performance, extended software support, or expandable storage for a large collection of photos and apps.

The Edge 2026’s biggest selling point is its size. If you’re tired of lugging ever-bigger smartphones around, its small and light design is a welcome alternative. You still get a generous screen, but without having to compromise with a massive handset.

There's more to like than just the form factor. The Motorola screen is complemented by a MediaTek Dimensity 7450 processor, while its triple rear camera system relies on a 50MP Sony LYTIA 710 sensor for main photography. That said, performance is middling, so this isn't the phone we'd recommend to demanding users or mobile gamers.

The numbers are adequate for everyday use. You get a 6.3-inch Extreme AMOLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate, 5,000mAh battery, 60W wired charging, and 15W wireless charging. The small screen and large battery capacity make it a good option for those who care more about battery life than raw processing power.

This is an especially juicy discount considering the $599.99 list price, it must be said. Taking $200 off that brings the phone down to $399.99, a much more reasonable proposition for shoppers looking for a smaller Android device. The Black Friday discount also ties the lowest price on record in Amazon’s price history.

But there are trade-offs. There’s no microSD slot, and the phone is capped at 128GB of non-expandable storage. Another problem is the short software support, especially if you’re one to hold onto your phones for a few years. Those are limitations to be aware of if you're a heavy photographer or someone who keeps their phone for the long haul.

item.title: Your Android phone could help you avoid expensive car repairs this winter, and TOPDON's Black Friday deals make it easier than ever
item.dc:content:
There's never a convenient time for your car to break down, but a freezing winter morning when you're already running late for work has to be among the worst possible scenarios.

Thankfully, modern automotive technology has made it a lot easier to understand what's going on with your vehicle, often without specialist knowledge or an expensive trip to the repair shop.

Tools once reserved for professional workshops can now connect directly to your smartphone and provide useful information about your car's condition through easy-to-use apps.

TOPDON is one of the companies making this technology more accessible, and offers everything from affordable Bluetooth diagnostic scanners to advanced equipment designed for professional mechanics.

This Black Friday, the company is launching a substantial sale across its automotive range, with promotional prices running from November 19 through November 30.

A little preparation can make winter driving considerably less stressful

One of the simplest ways to prepare for winter is to make sure your car's battery is in good condition before temperatures drop.

The TOPDON BT100 Battery Tester, available for $43.99 during Black Friday, provides a straightforward way to check the condition of a 12V battery without visiting a garage.

It can assess battery health and starting performance to help drivers determine whether a battery might need attention before it leaves them stranded.

Of course, even a well-maintained vehicle can experience an unexpected flat battery, which is why keeping a portable jump starter in the trunk is a sensible precaution.

The TOPDON JS2000 Pro combines a powerful 2,500A peak-output jump starter with a 16,000mAh battery, providing enough power to jump-start compatible vehicles without assistance from another driver.

It also doubles as a portable power bank for charging electronic devices, which could prove particularly useful if you're travelling somewhere remote and your phone is running low on power.

With its Black Friday price of $80.74, it's a practical addition to a winter emergency kit that could come in handy long after the colder months have passed.

Your smartphone can tell you more about your car than you might think

Modern vehicles are packed with electronics that continuously track how different components are performing, but drivers often have very little access to this information.

OBD2 diagnostic scanners can connect to your vehicle's onboard diagnostic port and retrieve fault codes to better understand potential problems with your car.

For Android users, the TOPDON CarPal is an especially interesting starting point because it uses Bluetooth to send information directly to your smartphone.

Through the companion app, you can access vehicle health information and diagnostic trouble codes without taking the car to the repair shop for a checkup.

At $37.97 during TOPDON's Black Friday promotion, the CarPal A is also the most affordable diagnostic scanner in the lineup.

Drivers who enjoy carrying out their own maintenance might prefer something more advanced, such as the TOPDON AD600S or AD800BT2, which offer deeper diagnostic capabilities and additional service functions. Both models also benefit from free lifetime software updates.

Thermal imaging opens up even more possibilities

Another interesting development in automotive diagnostics is the growing accessibility of thermal imaging technology, which can reveal unusual temperature differences that might indicate an underlying issue.

The TOPDON TC002C Duo connects directly to compatible USB-C Android smartphones, iPhones and tablets, essentially turning an everyday device into a portable thermal imaging camera.

It's useful for investigating potential overheating issues around vehicle components, but its applications extend well beyond automotive maintenance, as it can also identify heat-loss areas around your home.

The TC002C Duo is available for $229.89 during Black Friday, while TOPDON also offers standalone thermal cameras for users who prefer dedicated equipment.

Get your car winter-ready for less this Black Friday

TOPDON’s Black Friday promotion runs from November 19 to November 30, 2026 and covers automotive equipment for casual drivers and professional mechanics alike.

If you've been considering putting together a winter emergency kit or investing in diagnostic equipment, it's worth exploring TOPDON's Black Friday offers before the promotional period ends.

item.title: Android's sideloading freedom is about to get a lot more complicated worldwide
item.dc:content:
For quite a long time, Android has had one big advantage over iOS: you can install apps from basically anywhere, without asking Google's permission. That freedom is about to come with considerably more friction.

Google has confirmed that its developer verification requirements will begin rolling out globally in January 2027, making it harder to install apps from developers who haven’t registered with the company.

Announced in 2025, the policy requires Android app developers to verify their identities and register their applications with Google, regardless of where those applications are distributed. The new rules will also apply to third-party app marketplaces and independently distributed APKs.

Google is working with seven distributors, including Google Play, Samsung’s Galaxy Store, Honor, Oppo, Xiaomi, Transsion, and Vivo, to bring the requirements to more users.

Google says the changes are intended to make it more difficult for scammers and malicious developers to continue distributing harmful apps. The company says millions of applications have already been registered, representing more than 99% of Android app installs worldwide. The launch began on September 30, 2026, in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand.

Sideloading will become a much bigger hassle for Android users

But developers won’t be the only ones feeling the shift. To install unverified apps, you’ll have to take extra steps. You’ll have to authenticate your device and make sure you’re not being forced to change your security settings. After this, restart your phone and wait 24 hours before you can enable unrestricted sideloading.

Google does offer an advanced install option for power users who want to skip verification, but it’s not quite the one-tap experience Android enthusiasts have grown accustomed to.

There are also concessions for smaller developers. Free limited-distribution accounts allow students and hobbyists to share apps with up to 50 authorized devices without having to verify their identity with a government ID or pay registration fees. Google has also added APIs to make it easier for developers with multiple apps to register.

But the bigger question is what this change means for Android’s reputation as an open platform. Google says users can still choose where they download their apps from, but the freedom is made a lot less convenient by adding identity checks, restrictions on installation, and a mandatory waiting period.

After the global rollout, protections are expected to be available to all countries and installation sources over the span of a few months. Google documentation states that full enforcement is expected on March 1, 2027.

item.title: Why settle for a Kindle? This Android tablet is an e-reader and much more for under $200
item.dc:content:
If you've been thinking about buying a Kindle or another e-reader, you might want to take a look at this Android tablet before spending your money. The TCL NXTPAPER 11 Plus gives you a paper-like display that's designed to be easier on your eyes, but unlike a traditional Kindle, it can also do pretty much everything you'd expect from a regular Android tablet. And the best part? It's now available for less than $200.

NXTPAPER 11 Plus Android Tablet: was $279 now $199
The TCL NXTPAPER 11 Plus combines a paper-like display with the flexibility of a full Android tablet. It features an 11.5-inch 2.2K 120Hz screen, three display modes, 256GB of storage, and an 8,000mAh battery with 33W fast charging.View Deal

  • 20+ Black Friday 2026 deals for Android lovers

✅ Recommended if: You want a paper-like display for reading, prefer a larger screen for books and PDFs, or want an affordable Android tablet that handles streaming, browsing, and everyday tasks.

❌ Skip this deal if: You want the weeks-long battery life of a dedicated Kindle, prefer a smaller e-reader, or need a powerful tablet for demanding games and heavy multitasking.

TCL has been making NXTPAPER devices for a while now, and the NXTPAPER 11 Plus is one of the more interesting tablets in its lineup. Unlike other NXTPAPER tablets, this tablet lets you switch between three different modes, including Regular Mode, Color Paper Mode, and Ink Paper Mode, simply by pressing the dedicated NXTPAPER Key on the tablet.

You can use the regular mode when watching videos or browsing the web, switch to Color Paper Mode for a more comfortable reading experience, or use Ink Paper Mode for a more traditional black-and-white e-reader feel.

Speaking of display, the NXTPAPER 11 Plus comes with a 11.5-inch display with a 2.2K resolution and a smooth 120Hz refresh rate. That said, the best part of this tablet is probably its design.

It is only 0.26 inches thin and weighs around 1.08 pounds. That makes it easy to toss into your backpack before a flight or carry around throughout the day without adding much weight. TCL has also given it a metal body, so you're not getting a cheap-feeling plastic tablet despite the affordable price.

Battery life shouldn't be much of a concern either. The NXTPAPER 11 Plus packs a sizable 8,000mAh battery, which should be plenty for long reading sessions, watching movies, or getting through a day of regular use. And when you do need to charge it, there's support for up to 33W wired fast charging.

Of course, there are a few compromises at this price. The tablet is powered by the MediaTek Helio G100 chipset, which isn't exactly a flagship processor. It's perfectly reasonable for everyday tasks like reading, browsing, and streaming, but don't expect the same performance you'd get from a more flagship Samsung Galaxy tablet or iPad.

That said, if you're looking for a relatively inexpensive tablet this Black Friday that also doubles as an e-reader, this is probably one of the best deals you can get right now.

item.title: Lowest we've seen it—Pixel 11 Pro XL gets a huge 31% Black Friday price knock that's too hard to ignore
item.dc:content:
Google's Pixel 11 series was highly sought after this year. At times, it felt like there was more anticipation for this series than for the ones before it. Nevertheless, we'll still go over everything this phone has to offer in this massive Amazon deal.

Black Friday is about a week away, but that's not stopping Google's Pixel 11 Pro XL from dropping 31% to $899. This is the lowest we've seen it, and it's probably a good time to check out what it has to offer.

Pixel 11 Pro XL (Canyon): was $1299 now $899
It's hard to look away from this one. The Google Pixel 11 Pro XL is the lowest we've seen it at, with a 31% discount on Amazon. The phone drops by a whopping $400, and that includes a captivating 6.8-inch display and all of Google's Pixel magic.View Deal

There's a lot to cover, but the Pixel 11 Pro XL is ✅ recommended if you want the top of the line from Google's Pixel series. The 11 Pro XL offers the largest screen of its slab phones at 6.8 inches. Google keeps its iconic camera bar design with the 11 Pro XL; however, a standout feature is Pixel HiLight. This is a small, circular LED inside the camera bar that lights up for notifications. If someone is calling you, Pixel HiLight will let you know.

On the other hand, you'd likely ❌ skip this deal if you're a bit conscious about certain technical/hardware decisions. One of the Pixel 11 Pro XL's biggest drawbacks is its smaller battery than the Pixel 10 Pro XL's. Unfortunately, the cell drops from 5,200mAh to 5,115mAh. What's more, Google hasn't done a great job with the phone's PWM dimming. If you're prone to headaches or eye strain, the Pixel 11 Pro XL won't help.

Another major drawback for us is the price—the official price. Google raised prices this year for its Pixel 11 series, including the Pixel 11 Pro XL. This discounted price on Amazon looks all the more intriguing, remembering that.

There are aspects that we wish Google had done better on the Pixel 11 Pro XL. That goes without saying. However, there's plenty of good, too. If you're looking to snag this huge 31% discount on the Pixel 11 Pro XL from Amazon and make it your new daily driver, you'll find a pretty sweet camera experience. The Pixel 11 Pro XL feels like a return to the great cameras Google used to have on older Pixels.

A 50MP wide and 48MP ultrawide lens will carry you through a lot of your daily photography. Google has also included Magic Capture. To us, this is one of its standout features. Magic Capture helps ensure the best moments are captured, so you never forget them. If you're looking to capture smiles, laughter, or insane moments, Magic Capture does its best to solidify them. Even the video quality on the Pixel 11 Pro XL took a major step forward.

On the hardware side, Google integrated its Tensor G6 chip, which is pretty good. The chip is much better at helping users multitask between apps, and swiping/scrolling remains incredibly smooth. Qi2 wireless charging magnets are also integrated directly into the Pixel 11 Pro XL's body, so you won't need an external accessory.

item.dc:content:
Let's get something straight right off the bat: the Galaxy S26 FE beat the S26 Ultra to One UI 9. Amidst those heavy delays, Samsung's latest FE phone launched with its newest Android OS upgrade well ahead of its 2026 flagship Ultra.

Jokes aside, the Galaxy S26 FE is still a darn good phone for its price. Black Friday is roughly a week away, and Amazon's already knocked the phone down by 25%.

Samsung's latest FE model—the Galaxy S26 FE—is down 25%, dropping its price from $799 to $599. The phone comes with 256GB of storage, the latest Android 17 (One UI 9) software, and Galaxy AI.View Deal

If you're asking us, the Galaxy S26 FE is ✅ recommended if you want the latest tech on a budget. Keep in mind that the S26 FE is $799, but with this 25% deal, you'll get it for $599. If you want a slightly bigger phone, the S26 FE offers a 6.7-inch display that outshines many other midrange devices. One UI 9 (Android 17) is another plus, with various UI updates, smoother animations, and AI privacy alerts. Samsung will also support the Galaxy S26 FE with seven years of OS upgrades.

You should probably ❌ skip this deal if you're looking for a more robust phone. The Galaxy S26 FE is a mid-range phone, so its performance isn't top-tier. The phone features Samsung's Exynos 2500 SoC, and while the chip has improved over previous iterations, it may still struggle graphically. What's more, the S26 FE's camera system pales in comparison to Samsung's flagships, as its main highlight is a 50MP main sensor.

All in all, the Galaxy S26 FE is still a solid buy at 25% off. Samsung launched the phone this year at a price $50 higher than in previous years. So, seeing it at this discounted price is all the more enticing. Another thing to remember is that the phone's screen size matches the Galaxy S26 Plus—a flagship phone. Samsung tried to bridge the best of both worlds (midrange and flagship), and it does that fairly well.

There are some caveats, but with 256GB of internal storage and a 120Hz display refresh rate, the S26 FE's early Black Friday deal isn't that bad.

item.title: An Android phone with a built-in stylus for under $200? It must be Black Friday
item.dc:content:

Thankfully, Motorola has you covered with the Moto Stylus – one of the few budget-friendly models that comes with a pen. Now, the handset is cheaper than it's ever been on Amazon, with a Black Friday discount that takes it down to just $199.99 from $399.99.

Key specs:

🐲 Chipset: Snapdragon 6 Gen 3
🐄 RAM: 8GB
💾 Storage: 256GB
🔋 Battery: 5,000mAh
⭐ Star feature: Built-in stylus

Despite the low price, it's not a low-end phone by any means. It's got a bright AMOLED display at a butter-smooth 120Hz refresh rate, 8GB of RAM, and (in the case of this particular unit) 256GB of built-in storage. It's powered by the Qualcomm Snapdragon 6 Gen 3, which, while firmly a mid-range chip, delivers smooth day-to-day performance and casual gaming.

The real start of the show is that stylus, though, and you can pop it out for easy sketching or note-taking. Oh, and the phone is a cool textured blue color, helping it really stand out from the crowd.

  • Browse all the latest Black Friday Amazon deals

Moto G Stylus (2025): was $399.99 now $199.99
A decent mid-range phone that stands out thanks to its included stylus and current low price. This is the cheapest this model has ever been on Amazon, and a killer price for something with a decent chipset, 8GB of RAM, and 256GB of storage. There's also a microSD card slot, so you can add more room if you need it.View Deal

✅Recommended if: The Motorola Moto G Stylus is one of the few phone models that come with a built-in stylus and doesn't cost a fortune. If you're looking for a more affordable phone that lets you draw and take notes easily, then the Moto G Stylus is a serious contender.

item.title: Upgrading your home theater? Here are 10+ early Black Friday deals on our favorite TVs, soundbars, streaming devices, and more
item.dc:content:
Black Friday is one of those events that just shows how quickly the year flies by, and now we're about to enter the chaotic period once again. It's time to start hunting for the best offers.

The Best Black Friday Deals For Android Fans

Deals on tech are not few and far between, especially when it comes to devices that seriously upgrade your home theater setup. Have you been suffering from poor TV quality or below-average audio from your soundbar? This is where we come in handy.

If you've been meaning to upgrade, Black Friday 2026 is your time to do so, and some of our best soundbars and best Android TVs are already getting some huge price drops - and we're still a week away from the shopping event of the year. Notably, the Sonos Arc Ultra Soundbar is available at Amazon for $849 down from $1099, while Hisense's U8 Series ULED Mini-LED with Google TV is $749.99 from $1424.99.

But home theaters are so much more than your TV and soundbar combination. If you're really looking to take your setup to the next level, I strongly suggest looking into ambient lighting to really tie things together, and luckily, you can find some solid deals on our best smart LED light strips below.

QUICK LINKS TO THE BIG BLACK FRIDAY SALES

  • Amazon: Big savings on tech essentials
  • Best Buy: Half price TVs, laptops, gadgets and more
  • Walmart: Members get early access to giant savings

Today's best deals — Soundbars

Arc Ultra Soundbar: was $1099 now $849

It's still on the pricier side even with its Black Friday discount, but it's already beaten last season's price tag. If you're ready to take your home theater audio to the next level, this is the one to look out for. View Deal

Despite its size it still supports Dolby Atmos, with boosting seamless connectivity with other speakers in the Sonos family. It also doubles as a smart speaker, which is a welcomed bonus. View Deal

TV deals

Ultra: was $149 now $89

Smart lights deals

Floor Lamp 2: was $159.99 now $99.99
Our best floor lamp brightens up any room, setting the right ambience to fit the titles you're streaming during your movie nights. With Alexa compatibility, Govee's standing lamp has 82 scene modes, 10 music modes, and a higher brightness of up to 1,725 lumens, so its lighting can really stretch across wider spaces. View Deal

Envisual TV LED Backlight: was $169.99 now $79.99
TV backlights are a fun and creative way to integrate ambient lighting into your home theater setup, and Govee is a solid, affordable alternative to Philips Hue, which can be ridiculously expensive and require additional hardware. For less than $100, Govee's backlights have Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity, come with dual cameras, and can even be synced to music. View Deal

item.title: This family-friendly console offers classic Android games on your TV for less than half the price of a Nintendo Switch 2
item.dc:content:
If you're searching for a fun, family-friendly activity to keep everyone busy over the holidays, then look no further than the Nex Playground.

This adorable little game console is now just $209, down from $299, on Amazon thanks to an early Black Friday deal.

It runs a customized Android-based operating system designed with kids in mind, offering convenient controller-free motion controls. It comes with a selection of five games built in, too, giving you plenty to play out of the box.

This includes some modern versions of classic mobile games, like a motion-controlled version of Fruit Ninja that's an awful lot of fun.

More games are then available via a relatively cheap $89 per year Play Pass subscription, with franchises like Barbie, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, and How to Train Your Dragon all represented in the line-up.

  • Browse all the latest Black Friday Amazon deals

The Nex Playground is a compact game console designed for families and children. It's easy to set up and features easy-to-understand motion controls that encourage movement. With support for up to four players, it comes bundled with a selection of kidSafe+ COPPA certified titles, including versions of hits like Fruit Ninja.View Deal

✅Recommended if: You're after a family-friendly console that can keep the kids entertained and comes in cheaper than other options. At this discounted price, the Nex Playground costs less than half that of the Nintendo Switch 2 — which retails for $499.99. You don't even have to splash out for extra games or controllers, as five titles are built-in and you can control everything through motion.

❌Skip this deal if: You're after a more traditional gaming console. The Nex Playground is recommended for children between five and ten, so while it is a lot of fun, older kids will likely prefer a more traditional gaming console.

item.title: Amazon just upgraded its entire tablet line to Android — and there are already huge savings on all of the new models for Black Friday
item.dc:content:
Amazon recently revamped its entire tablet line, ditching the Fire name and operating system in favor of a smattering of proper Android tablets. The Amazon Alexa Tablet family covers all form factors and usage needs, ranging from the affordable and compact Amazon Alexa Tablet 8 all the way to the high-end Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro.

The best part? They're all heavily discounted for Black Friday. The entry-level Alexa Tablet 8 now costs just $149.99 (down from $229.99), with a portable 8.7-inch form factor, 4GB of RAM, and 64GB of on-board storage.

If you want something a little more premium, then there's the Amazon Alexa Tablet 11 at just $219.99 (was $329.99), which upgrades the display to an 11-inch 2.5K panel and boosts the RAM to 8GB for smoother multitasking performance.

Finally, there's the top-of-the-line Alexa Tablet 12 Pro on sale for $449.99 (was $549.99), with its 12-inch 2.8K display boasting an innovative Nanomatte coating, which dramatically cuts down glare. This is on top of a 120Hz refresh rate, 8GB of RAM, and 12GB of storage.

All three models run Android, with full support for all of your favorite Google Play Store apps. Read on for everything you need to know.

  • Browse all the latest Black Friday Amazon deals

Alexa Tablet 8: was $229.99 now $149.99
This entry-level tablet is a great choice for families or those after something more compact. It's powered by an 8-core chip and 4GB of RAM, with an 8.7-inch HD screen. Despite the low price, its case is constructed with aluminum rather than plastic.View Deal

The Amazon Alexa Tablet 11 upgrades the screen to a larger and higher-resolution 11-inch 2.5K panel with a 90Hz refresh rate, which is better suited for media consumption. At just over $200, it's fantastic value if you're seeking an all-round media machine.View Deal

Alexa Tablet 12 Pro: was $549.99 now $449.99
This is Amazon's highest-end Android tablet, geared towards powerful multitasking performance. The 2.8K Nanomatte screen cuts down on glare, while 128GB of storage offers plenty of room for downloaded apps.View Deal

✅Recommended if: The Amazon Alexa Tablet line is worthwhile if you're searching for some good-value Android tablets. I can't think of any model from a major brand that delivers more bang for your buck than the affordable Alexa Tablet 8, while the mid-range Alexa Tablet 11 offers plenty of meaningful screen upgrades for an excellent viewing experience. The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, meanwhile, delivers strong performance and a spacious screen for more serious productivity.

Although the Android operating system of the Amazon Alexa Tablet line is a lot more open than FireOS ever was, with full support for Google Play out of the box, it still comes pre-loaded with Amazon apps like Prime Video, Kindle, and Amazon Luna. There are better options out there if you are already all-in on a different ecosystem.

item.title: Honor's new smartwatch has the brightest display I've ever seen on a wearable — beating the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 at a fraction of the price
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Honor just launched a new smartwatch: the Honor Watch 6 Pro
  • It features an impressively bright 5,500-nit AMOLED display, which makes it one of the brightest on the market, and 18 days of battery life
  • It also comes in at just £229.99 thanks to a launch discount

Honor just launched its latest smartwatch, the Honor Watch 6 Pro, and it looks like a formidable contender in the wearable space.

Its standout spec is a 1.5-inch AMOLED display capable of delivering a staggering 5,500nits of brightness. This is, as far as I can see per readily available spec information, the brightest smartwatch display on the market right now, beating the 5,000 nits offered by the high-end Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra2 and Garmin fenix 8 Pro.

This should keep it legible in even the harshest sunlight, which every smartwatch user will know can sometimes be a challenge. Despite this brightness, Honor claims that the 515mAh battery will provide up to 18 days of typical usage.

The Honor Watch 6 Pro boasts a 5ATM water resistance (which should make it usable at a depth of up to 50 meters). This is in addition to IP68, IP69, and IP69K dust and water resistance ratings.

You're also getting a wealth of sensors for comprehensive health tracking, including an accelerometer, gyroscope, and optical heart rate sensor, plus dual-frequency GPS for accurate positioning. You can use the watch for contactless payments thanks to its built-in NFC capabilities, too.

All of this comes in an attractive package inspired by premium watchmaking, with a stainless steel front case and nanocrystalline ceramic bezel.

Android Central's take: The price is right

In my eyes, Honor is one of the most exciting smartphone brands right now. Originally a Huawei subsidiary, the company split off in 2020 and has steadily grown into a serious competitor to the big names like Samsung, Google, Motorola, and Xiaomi. I have tested countless smartphones and tablets, but it's the Honor ones that I keep coming back to because of their high specs and quirky phone designs.

Honor frequently undercuts its competition with attractive discount coupons and a bombardment of freebies too, and the Honor Watch 6 Pro is no exception. Its price technically starts at £339.99 (that's roughly $450), but the brand is already offering a £100 discount to celebrate the launch, which takes it down to just £229.99 (just above $300).

You also get a free pair of clip-on earbuds, a bonus brown watch strap, and a complimentary 'worry-free' service plan that offers one free repair for screen or liquid damage, as well as an extended warranty service (you can read the full terms of that here).

It's a limited-time offer, but I expect it or similar discounts to return regularly in the coming months and, at this price, the value proposition is excellent on paper. It's going head-to-head with the likes of the Samsung Galaxy Watch8 or Huawei Watch Fit 5 Pro, and beats both on battery life and screen brightness.

I also think the design of the Honor Watch 6 Pro is more attractive, as it looks a lot less like a traditional smartwatch than those two alternatives, but that, of course, comes down to personal preference.

It's not a complete slam dunk, though, as Honor loses to Samsung when it comes to availability, as its products are not officially sold in the US. You also have the matter of Honor's MagicOS software, which tends to be less polished than Samsung's One UI Watch in my experience.

I've reached out to Honor to request a unit to see how it stacks up in the real world, so expect a full review soon.
